newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa, Rwanda agree to strengthen cooperation.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa, Rwanda agree to strengthen cooperation.

text.p: South Africa and Rwanda signed a declaration of intent on Friday to strengthen economic, scientific and technical cooperation between the two countries.

The agreement was signed by Rwanda's foreign minister Anastase Gasana and South Africa's deputy foreign minister Aziz Pahad in Pretoria at the end of a week-long visit by a Rwandan government delegation headed by Vice President Paul Kagame.
South Africa has said it will send an economic team to Kigali next month to help rebuild the country's fiscal infrastructure, including budget formulation and debt management.

Rwanda's economy was crippled by a genocide in 1994 in which 800,000 mostly Tutsis were slaughtered. It triggered the takeover of Rwanda by the Tutsi-dominated Rwandese Patriotic Front, sending millions of Hutus fleeing to eastern Zaire.
Resettlement of the millions of refugees in their homeland is a challenge for the Rwandan government, which says it still faces security threats from armed Hutu militia living among the refugees.
"We recognise the need to broaden existing contacts and to explore new cooperation possibilities in a variety of fields," the agreement stated.
The two governments have agreed to cooperate in the fields of finance, trade and industry, transport, water management and security and defence matters.
Pahad told a news conference South Africa would announce shortly the outcome of a review to lift a moratorium on arms sales to Rwanda.
He said the decision was being considered by South Africa's National Conventional Arms Control Committee (NCACC).
"We have been talking about lifting the moratorium, but that decision will be made very shortly by the NCACC," Pahad said.
South Africa cancelled a proposed 87 million rand ($19 million) arms deal with Rwanda last year pending the review.
